# Test: gyms drop minerals on kill

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic gym tests that fail while the gyms do not drop minerals, pinning the behaviour the gym-wiring task must deliver.

## Required coverage

- Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row (via the shared destruction path and via the EXPLODE button) increases the live mineral count by exactly one at the asteroid's position.
- A large/medium asteroid splits into its children without a direct mineral drop.
- No double drop: a single destruction produces exactly one drop (not one per path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the gym drop behaviour; `npm test` for the gym suites passes.
- Tests assert the drop position and count, not merely that the count increased, and are deterministic (seeded RNG).
- Tests fail before the gym-wiring task lands and pass after it.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`

# Shared player-control step across all scenes

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 1 & 11).

## Summary

The sequence *input → tick weapon timers → apply P5 speed/fire-rate multipliers → physics → auto-fire* is re-implemented in `PlayScene.tick`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymWeapons.tick`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` and `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`, and `GymPlayer.update` inlines the scheme→input mapping instead of the shared `_readPlayerInput`. Extract one `_tickPlayer(dt)` (and keep `_readPlayerInput`) in `CombatCoreScene` so every scene advances the player identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatCoreScene` owns a single `_tickPlayer(dt)` that performs, in the same order every frame: `tickWeaponTimers`, live `setSpeedMultiplier`/`setFireRateMultiplier` from the effects registry, `_readPlayerInput`→`setInput`, `physicsTick`, and `_autoFire`. `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` call it instead of their local copy. Verified by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC2** — `GymPlayer` consumes the shared input mapping (calls `_readPlayerInput` or an extracted shared input helper) and no longer inlines the `fourDirHandler`/`asteroidsHandler` branch. Verified by a source guard and by `GymPlayer.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC3** — Timed-weapon expiry, P5 multipliers and auto-fire ordering are identical in the game and every gym for the same input and `dt`. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test booting `PlayScene` and a gym, applying a P5 effect and asserting the same speed/fire-rate outcome.
- [ ] **AC4** — `GymPowerUpsCombat` no longer uses a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the player path; the player is advanced from the supplied `dt` (the enemy-clock fix is child #2).
- [ ] **AC5** — All existing scene suites pass unchanged; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard covers `_tickPlayer`.
- [ ] **AC6** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4.
- [ ] **AC7** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC7)** — [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — new shared `_tickPlayer(dt)`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — consume the shared step.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — coverage.

## Open questions

- **OQ8 (from epic):** should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal? *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper.*

## Plan — changelog

- 2026-09-26 — `/skill:plan AH-0MUII39KX007YUQ0`: autoplan pre-check returned `decision: skip` (placeholder effort Extra Small / risk Low). Planning auto-completed via the six automated review stages. No child items were created: the parent epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` already decomposed register gaps 1 & 11 into this leaf task, and its ACs contain the test/verification obligations. No blocking clarifications were required; clarifications and one flagged AC wording issue are recorded below.

## Plan — automated review summary

Retained as a leaf task for direct implementation (measurable ACs + minimal implementation sketch):

- **Requirements & AC alignment:** AC1–AC7 trace to epic gaps 1 (player-control step duplicated) and 11 (`GymPlayer` not on the shared control core). AC1 names four consumers; AC2 covers `GymPlayer`; AC4 covers `GymPowerUpsCombat`; together they cover every consumer named in the summary. OQ8 is answered by AC2.
- **Completeness:** `## Acceptance Criteria` is present and the `## Key Files` paths are syntactically valid; all 11 referenced files exist at HEAD (`7bfe98f`).
- **Sequencing & dependencies:** no children. This item is the prerequisite (epic child #1) for boss integration (child #6) and the parity guard (child #10). Tests are embedded in AC1–AC5, so the test-first intent is satisfied without separate children.
- **Scope sizing:** one focused refactor (add `_tickPlayer`, migrate six scenes, tests, docs) — a deliverable increment.
- **Acceptance & testability:** all ACs are pass/fail; AC3 (cross-scene equivalence) and AC5 (duplicate-body guard) name automated verification.
- **Polish & handoff:** description is actionable; the Key Files list matches the consumer set.
- **AC coverage review:** `run_coverage_review` returned `recommendation: proceed` (leaf item; no children).

## Plan — clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: "OQ8 — should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal?" Answer (epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`): *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper; it need not add enemies.* Final accepted: **yes** — AC2 requires `GymPlayer` to consume the shared input mapping.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Is the sequence described in the summary actually one identical sequence in every named scene?" Research (HEAD `7bfe98f`; read of `PlayScene.tick` L557–572, `GymFormationScene.tick` L1299–1318, `GymWeapons.tick` L178–195, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` L154–170, `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick` L258–275): the scenes run **subsets with different ordering**, not identical copies — `PlayScene` runs tickWeaponTimers → multipliers → `_handleTeleport` → input → physics → auto-fire; `GymFormationScene` runs timers → multipliers → input → physics → auto-fire with teleport later; `GymWeapons` omits the P5 multipliers; `GymPowerUpsUtility` omits tickWeaponTimers and auto-fire; `GymPowerUpsCombat` omits timers, multipliers and auto-fire. Resolution (epic assumption, "the shipped game is canonical"): the shared `_tickPlayer(dt)` runs the full ordered sequence and each gym's absent feature resolves to a no-op (multiplier 1, empty weapon list). Recorded as an implementation assumption; if a test shows a behaviour change in those gyms the difference must be recorded in the epic and approved.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does `GymPowerUpsCombat` use a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the *player* path (AC4)?" Research: the only fixed 16 ms step is `_nextFireTime += 16` inside `_tickScouts` (`GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` L424), which is the **enemy-fire** clock and belongs to epic child #2 (`AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46`, "Shared enemy-fire dispatch using the real scene clock"); the player path already advances from the supplied `dt`. **OPEN QUESTION (AC4 wording):** AC4 should be read as "the `GymPowerUpsCombat` player path uses the supplied `dt`" (already true); the 16 ms enemy clock is fixed by child #2, not by this item. Intent is clear enough to implement; the wording is flagged for correction rather than rewritten here (rewriting could change intent).

**OQ-NOTE (effort/risk):** the autoplan pre-check generated a zeroed placeholder estimate (O=M=P=0, 0.00 h → Extra Small / Low) because `plan_helpers.run_effort_and_risk` submits a fixed `{o:0,m:0,p:0}` payload. Treat the `effort`/`risk` fields as a placeholder; `<WIP-id>` should receive a genuine `/skill:effort-and-risk` estimate before implementation is dispatched.

# Ships drop minerals (AH-0MULUOZQP009GRWX)

## Problem statement

When a non-asteroid enemy that has absorbed minerals is destroyed, the game
re-drops a **floored fraction (25–50 %)** of what it absorbed. Because the
count is floored, an enemy that absorbed only one or two minerals drops
**nothing**, and the distribution under-rewards the player relative to the
intent. The re-drop should instead add a **random bonus of 0.25–1.25** to the
absorbed count and **round to the nearest integer**, so every destroyed
mineral-carrying enemy reliably returns roughly what it held (and may
occasionally return slightly more).

## Users

- **As a player**, when I destroy an enemy that has been hoovering up my
  minerals, I want it to release back about the minerals it absorbed (plus a
  small random bonus) so the effort to shoot it feels rewarded and
  predictable.
- **As a game designer**, I want the re-drop amount to stay a single
  configurable rule that the game and every gym consume, so the behaviour
  cannot drift between them.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New formula** — `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount(rng)` returns
   `Math.round(collected + random(0.25, 1.25))`, where the bonus is drawn from
   the injected rng in `[0.25, 1.25]` (one draw). At the extremes,
   `rng() = 0` → `round(collected + 0.25)` and `rng() → 1` →
   `round(collected + 1.25)`.
   *Verification:* unit tests over several collected counts at both rng
   extremes.
2. **No upper cap** — the re-drop is no longer clamped to the collected count,
   so an enemy that absorbed `N` minerals may drop up to
   `round(N + 1.25)`, and never less than `round(N + 0.25)`.
   *Verification:* unit tests showing the upper bound exceeds `N` for
   `N = 1, 2` and the lower bound holds.
3. **Empty enemy can occasionally drop** *(revised per producer review 2026-10-02)* — an enemy
   that absorbed nothing still draws the bonus; `round(0 + random(0.25, 1.25))` yields `0` or `1`,
   so it drops nothing most of the time but may occasionally drop a single mineral.
   *Verification:* unit tests at both rng extremes for `collected = 0`.
4. **Shared rule preserved (game/gym parity)** — `resolveMineralKillDrops`
   (consumed by both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`) spawns exactly
   `mineralRedropCount(rng)` scattered minerals at the death site with no
   divergent copy of the calculation.
   *Verification:* the shared-helper tests and the gym re-drop test are updated
   to the new rule; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard in
   `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` passes.
5. **Tunables renamed to match the new semantics** —
   `mineralRedropFractionMin/Max` become `mineralRedropBonusMin/Max`
   (defaults `0.25` / `1.25`), persisted and loaded with corrupt-value
   fallback; legacy persisted configs (schema v1/v2) migrate without carrying
   stale fraction values.
   *Verification:* `rules.test.ts` covers defaults, save/load round-trip,
   invalid-value fallback and legacy migration.
6. **Documentation updated** — the rule, the removed cap and the renamed
   tunables are reflected in GDD §4.1 E7 and §4.4.1, the module-tree entries
   and the README mineral section, plus the affected code/module comments.
   *Verification:* doc review; no remaining "25–50 %" claims for this rule.
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new behaviour.
   *Verification:* run the full suite and all quality checks green.

## Constraints

- **UK English** in all written output.
- **Single shared implementation** — the calculation must stay in
  `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount` (reached through
  `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`); the game and every gym must not gain
  a private copy (enforced by the repo-wide parity guard).
- **Testability** — `mineralRedropCount(rng)` keeps its injectable rng and one
  draw per call so seeded tests stay deterministic.
- **No new gameplay surface** — no changes to scatter radius, asteroid drops,
  collection, the hold or the HUD.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `mineralRedropCount(rng)` computes
  `[floor(N × mineralRedropFractionMin), floor(N × mineralRedropFractionMax)]`
  (0.25/0.5) and draws an integer inside it, clamped to `N`.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — the shared kill-drop rule; delegates
  the non-asteroid count to `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount` and the scatter to
  `scatterMineralDrops` (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`).
- `src/core/rules.ts` — `mineralRedropFractionMin/Max` = 0.25/0.5,
  `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`, `coerceFraction` (range `[0, 1]`).
- Docs and tests assert the **25–50 %** rule and the **never-exceed** cap
  (`docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1/§4.4.1, `README.md`,
  `BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts`, `mineralKillDrops.test.ts`,
  `Harvester.test.ts`, `GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `rules.test.ts`).

## Desired change

- Replace the formula with `Math.round(collected + random(0.25, 1.25))` and
  drop the upper cap.
- Rename the tunables to `mineralRedropBonusMin/Max` with defaults
  0.25/1.25, bump the rules schema to v3 and migrate legacy configs, adding
  non-negative coercion suitable for the wider range.
- Update the shared-helper comments, tests and documentation to describe the
  additive bonus and nearest-integer rounding.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — new `mineralRedropCount` formula and updated
  JSDoc.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — renamed tunables, new defaults/constants, schema v3
  and migration/coercion.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — rule description in the module
  header (logic unchanged; still delegates).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — rewrite the re-drop
  distribution tests for the new formula and removed cap.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — update expected counts at the
  rng extremes.
- `src/entities/Harvester.test.ts` — update the Harvester re-drop test.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — update the non-asteroid
  re-drop test (remove the never-exceed assertion).
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — defaults, round-trip, invalid fallback and legacy
  migration for the renamed tunables.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.1 E7, §4.4.1 and the module tree.
- `README.md` — mineral rule/tunable lines.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — *Asteroids drop collectable minerals…* (parent
  feature that introduced enemy absorption and re-drop).
- **AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB** — *Gym asteroids do not drop minerals — share the
  mineral kill-drop code with the game* (created the shared rule this change
  modifies).
- **AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA** — *Mineral rules tunables and per-enemy mineral
  count* (introduced the tunables being renamed).
- **AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM** — *Test: Enemy mineral count and re-drop
  distribution* (the tests being updated).
- **AH-0MUJRVZP2002G8GC** — *Shared mineral-seek seam parity* (related shared
  mineral seam; completed).
- **AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX** — *Pluggable power-up choice strategy and
  permanent-effect support* (adjacent mineral-hold/power-up path; completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (superseded 2026-10-02):** the `mineralCount <= 0 → 0` guard was
  **removed** on producer review — a ship that absorbed nothing still draws the
  bonus and may occasionally drop a single mineral. The bare formula now applies
  universally; only asteroids keep an explicit zero override.
- **Assumption:** the tunables are renamed to `mineralRedropBonusMin/Max`
  (defaults 0.25/1.25) rather than keeping the now-misleading
  `…Fraction…` names, with a schema bump to v3 and an explicit migration.
- **Risk:** removing the cap changes the mineral economy (destroyed enemies
  return ~everything they absorbed, plus a little), which can fill the hold
  faster and yield more power-ups. **Mitigation:** the increase is bounded
  (≤ ~1 mineral per kill on average, plus rounding) and remains tunable.
- **Risk:** renaming persisted-rule keys could silently reset a designer's
  custom values. **Mitigation:** version-aware migration plus tests proving
  legacy configs migrate to defaults and current configs round-trip.
- **Risk:** `Math.round` ties round toward `+∞`; harmless here because the
  bonus is always positive and non-tied values dominate.
- **Scope creep (out of scope):** changes to scatter radius, asteroid drop
  counts, collection, HUD or audio/visual juice. Record separately as linked
  work items if raised.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which exact formula should replace the current 25–50 % rule?
  (A: `round(collected × random(0.25, 1.25))`; B: literal
  `round(collected + random(0.25, 1.25))`; C: other)
  — **Answer (operator, interactive):** *"B"* — add a random 0.25–1.25 to the
  collected count, then round to the nearest integer.
- **Q:** Should the drop still never exceed the collected count?
  (A: keep the cap; B: remove the cap)
  — **Answer (operator, interactive):** *"B"* — remove the cap; a destroyed
  enemy may drop more minerals than it collected.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX** – Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support (completed)
- **AH-0MUH1LEDQ0064J78** – [test-failure] PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — asteroid integration > AC6 — the wave clears only after ALL split children are destroyed (no stall, no early clear) — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V** – Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: absorbed, absorption, acceptance, add, adding (+272 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mubvgi62004ed9q, 0muhmt5jc004wrsb, absorbed, absorption, add (+254 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: absorbed, add, adding, already, always (+235 more)


---

## Reconciliation (2026-10-01)

All parent acceptance criteria are delivered in commit 278208dd, with the intermittent gym mineral-test fix in d686e01a. Five children (AH-0MUNB0ZVF009L7GY, AH-0MUNB10XB004O78F, AH-0MUNB11XB0074L52, AH-0MUNB12YT0006HDB, AH-0MUNB141P008X9B9) had been regressed to open/blocked by an apparent worklog data restore; they were restored to completed/in_review to match the delivered commits. The six pending in-main-slot child audits were performed and persisted, and the full suite was verified green at HEAD e26b62fe (120 files / 2683 tests).

Final verification (2026-10-02): mineral tests green; children audited Ready=Yes; full suite green at HEAD f4353700 (120 files / 2683 tests).

# Intake Brief — Advance waves on timer expiration

- **Type:** bug
- **Priority:** high
- **Stage:** idea

## Summary

Replace the wave-timeout penalty in the game and all enemy gyms. When the timer expires, surviving non-asteroid enemies no longer detonate or cost a life — they simply persist into the next wave (or gym respawn) as active, gating threats that the player must destroy.

## Problem Statement

When the per-wave time limit elapses, every surviving non-asteroid enemy is destroyed with a 10x explosion and the player loses one life (AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6, shipped v0.1.4). This punitive wipe makes a timeout effectively fatal and forces the player to start the wave fresh. The intended design is that surviving enemies should carry over.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** wants a timeout that adds pressure rather than punishment.
  - "As a player, I want a timeout to leave surviving enemies on the field, so I feel time pressure rather than being unfairly reset."
- **Gym players:** gyms should mirror the game's carry-over behaviour.
  - "As a gym player, I want timeouts to behave the same way as in the game."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Game: no detonation, no life loss on timeout.** Surviving non-asteroid enemies persist when timer expires. Player retains all lives. Timer resets for next wave.
2. **Game: survivors gate the next wave.** Carried-over enemies count toward the next wave's alive target. Next wave clears only when both new spawns AND carried-over enemies are destroyed.
3. **Game: survivors are fully active.** Carried-over ships move and attack through the 3s transition pause until destroyed. Asteroids persist independently.
4. **Game: survivors persist across levels and into the boss.** Universal carry-over rule.
5. **Gyms: no detonation, spawn fresh formation.** Survivors persist. After 3s respawn countdown, a fresh formation is spawned alongside survivors; both must be cleared.
6. **Shared code path.** Both `PlayScene._timeoutWave` and `GymFormationScene._onWaveTimeout` updated. The shared detonation helper becomes a no-op.
7. **Documentation updated.** GDD, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md, code comments.
8. **Full test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- Gym-game parity mandatory. Documented divergence only.
- Asteroid persistence (AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO) must not break.
- Wave-timeout bar remains; resets at each new wave.
- No new config keys needed.

## Existing State

- `PlayScene._timeoutWave()` detonates survivors, calls `_loseLife(false)`, advances wave/level.
- `GymFormationScene._onWaveTimeout()` detonates survivors, starts respawn countdown.
- `core/waveTimeout.ts` defines `detonateWaveTimeoutSurvivors()`, `WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE=10`.
- GDD and ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md document detonation behaviour.

## Desired Change

- Replace `_timeoutWave`: no detonation, no life loss, register survivors with WaveManager for gating, advance wave/level, reset timer.
- Replace gym `_onWaveTimeout`: no detonation, spawn fresh formation after 3s countdown.
- Update shared helper to be no-op.
- Update documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_timeoutWave()`, `_advanceAfterTimeout()`, `_advanceWaveTimer()`
- `src/scenes/core/waveTimeout.ts` — `detonateWaveTimeoutSurvivors()`, constants
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_onWaveTimeout()`, `_startRespawnCountdown()`
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — may need timeout-aware advance seam
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 wave-timeout
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §2.6 gym wave-timeout

## Related Work

- AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 — Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x scale (shipped v0.1.4) — **directly superseded**
- AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO — Asteroids do not need to be cleared for wave completion (persistence precedent)
- AH-0MUNR5LM1004B223 — Add wave-timeout to all enemy gyms (parity)
- AH-0MUK5ONAA0007YEX — Shared wave-timeout helper for gym-parity
- AH-0MU7JTEA6002GE37 — PlayScene fine-tuning (timer was per-wave, resets each wave)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** If survivors persist across levels into the boss, the boss fight becomes significantly harder if enemies carry over — this is by design but worth testing.
- **Assumption:** Carried-over enemies retain their current health, position, movement pattern, and attack state (no reset).
- **Assumption:** The WaveManager's `registerDynamicSpawn` or a similar seam can accommodate timeout-carried enemies. If not, a new `adoptCarriedSurvivors` method is needed.
- **Assumption:** The gym respawn system can handle spawning a new formation into a field that already has live enemies.
- **Failure mode:** If survivors are not registered with WaveManager, the next wave could clear prematurely (survivors not counted).
- **Failure mode:** If survivors persist into the boss indefinitely, a player who times out many waves could face a very large boss encounter.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should the life penalty be removed?" — Answer (operator): "a) Yes, remove life penalty entirely — timeout just advances to next wave." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "How should surviving ships behave in the next wave?" — Answer (operator): "a) Yes — survivors persist into the next wave exactly where they are." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What should happen with the wave timer bar on timeout?" — Answer (operator): "a) Reset at the start of the next wave." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Do carried-over ships gate the next wave?" — Answer (operator): "b) Yes — they are added to the next wave's roster and must also be destroyed." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should the change apply to gyms?" — Answer (operator): "a) Yes — update all wave-timeout gyms." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "How should survivors behave during transition countdown?" — Answer (operator): "b) Continue moving and firing like a live threat." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Do survivors persist across level boundaries and into the boss?" — Answer (operator): "a) Persist everywhere." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What should a gym's timeout do (no detonation)?" — Answer (operator): "a) Keep survivors and spawn fresh formation after 3s countdown." Source: interactive reply.

# Weapon Leveling (AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Today a weapon power-up is binary: collecting a weapon drop **adds** Spread/Dual/Rapid to the active set for 10 seconds, and nothing about a weapon can ever improve. This makes repeated pickups of the same weapon feel flat and leaves no build-progression loop within a run. We want weapons that are **constantly upgradable**: each weapon carries a level, and every level changes a set of tunable variables (fire rate, projectile count, size, pattern, damage type, AoE, status effects, …) so a small catalogue can yield a large space of unique, scaling weapons.

## Users and user stories

- **Player (temporary upgrades):** "As a player, collecting the same weapon drop again should make that weapon stronger, so that my weapon fires faster / more projectiles / larger bullets as the run progresses."
- **Player (permanent upgrades):** "As a player, spending a mineral hold-full choice on a weapon should permanently raise its level for the rest of the run, so surviving longer compounds into a stronger build."
- **Designer:** "As a designer, I want the upgrade variables defined as a data-driven catalogue with a diminishing-returns curve, so I can create and tune unique weapons without new bespoke code."
- **Developer/tuner:** "As a developer, I want a weapon-leveling gym that demonstrates the system, so I can tune the curve and verify gym↔game parity."

## Acceptance Criteria

> Scope note (producer-confirmed): this is an **implementation epic** targeting **MVP-partial** — a demonstrable vertical slice that plans for the full variable space but only needs to implement enough variables to prove the concept.

- **AC1 — Design & variable catalogue.** A documented weapon-leveling design exists (Game Design Document + code catalogue) that enumerates **at least 12 tunable upgrade variables** across the space of fire rate, projectile count, spread/pattern, projectile size, projectile speed, lifetime/range, damage, piercing, bounce, homing, AoE radius/falloff, status effects (hot/cold/electric), chain, crit, split-on-hit/expiry and knockback, together with the diminishing-returns level curve.
- **AC2 — Persistent per-weapon levels.** Each weapon carries a **run-scoped integer level**; collecting a temporary weapon drop increases that weapon's level and (re)activates it under the existing timed semantics. The level **persists for the run** (including across a weapon timing out) and resets only on run restart.
- **AC3 — Permanent mineral choice levels a weapon.** A hold-full mineral choice can **permanently** level up a weapon using the existing permanent-choice semantics; the offered options reflect current weapon levels.
- **AC4 — Leveled effects applied consistently (gym↔game parity).** At least **four** upgrade variables measurably change weapon behaviour at higher levels, and the same level-resolution code path is used by the shipped `PlayScene` and by the gyms (no divergent copies), verified by the duplicate-body/equivalence guard.
- **AC5 — Indefinite levels with diminishing returns.** Levels are unbounded; every variable's effective value is monotonic non-decreasing in level and asymptotically bounded by a finite cap (diminishing returns). Verified by unit/property tests over a wide level range.
- **AC6 — Beat-grid invariant preserved.** Any fire-rate upgrade keeps every shot on the shared 80 BPM beat grid — fire rates remain exact beat subdivisions and the catalogue-wide `isOnBeatGrid` invariant holds for every weapon at every level (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- **AC7 — HUD + gym demonstration.** The HUD displays each active weapon's level, and a dedicated weapon-leveling gym scene demonstrates temporary and permanent leveling interactively.
- **AC8 — Testing/validation.** Unit, integration and parity tests cover level resolution, curve monotonicity/caps, weapon-drop leveling, permanent-choice leveling, HUD readout and the gym demonstration.
- **AC9 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC10 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour must live once in `src/scenes/core/` and be consumed by both game and gyms; an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in both. Gyms that exercise weapons must be updated in the same change.
- **Beat-grid invariant (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B):** fire rates are derived from `beatSubdivisionMs`; an upgrade must not produce an off-grid interval.
- **Run-scoped:** levels are per-run state, cleared on reset/restart (mirrors the existing permanent/power-up semantics); never written to the leaderboard unless explicitly decided.
- **MVP-partial:** only enough variables to demonstrate; the remaining catalogue is planned/specified but not all implemented.
- **Reuse:** extend `src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/entities/Player.ts` and the shared combat core — do not fork weapon logic into scenes.
- **No new weapon entities required for MVP:** the shipped catalogue (cannon/spread/dual/rapid) may keep its identity, with levels layered on top.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `WeaponDefinition` (id, name, description, offsets, sideOffsets, fireRateMs, bulletColor, bulletShape, bulletSize, bulletLifetime), `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` (cannon/spread/dual/rapid), `weaponFireRateMs`, `isOnBeatGrid`, `bulletForShot`/`allBulletsForShot`/`createBulletsFromHeading`, `weaponDropOrder`. No level dimension.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `_permanentWeapons` (cannon + chosen permanents), `_weaponTimers` (per-weapon 10 s countdown), `equipWeapon(id, permanent)`, `resetWeapon()`, `tickWeaponTimers(dt)`, phase-locked `tryFire(dt)` on the shared `BeatClock`, `getWeaponDef(id)` returning the static catalogue entry, `_effectiveInterval` (applies the P5 fire-rate multiplier).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_autoFire(dt)` calls `player.tryFire`, then `player.getWeaponDef(weaponId)` → `createBulletsFromHeading` → `spawnPlayerBullet(x, y, vx, vy, color, lifetime)`. Single shared path for game + gyms.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `CHOICE_POOL` (P3–P9 + spread/dual/rapid), pluggable `ChoiceStrategy`, default `randomChoiceStrategy` drawing **3** distinct options.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` + `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — hold-full pause overlay and `applyMineralChoiceReward` (permanent `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect`/`applyWeapon`, `Player.equipWeapon(id, true)`).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — one row per active effect and one row per equipped weapon (reads the shared `EffectsRegistry`).
- GDD §4.4 (power-ups/weapons) and §4.5 (minerals, hold, choice).
- Gym scenes: `GymWeapons`, `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymFormationScene` (shared).

## Desired change

1. **Level dimension in the catalogue.** Introduce a data-driven upgrade spec (`WeaponUpgradeSpec`/level table) keyed by `WeaponId`, describing how each variable scales per level with caps/diminishing returns, plus a pure `resolveWeaponAtLevel(def, level) → WeaponDefinition` (or equivalent `WeaponLevelStats`) resolver.
2. **Per-weapon level state on `Player`.** Track `Map<WeaponId, number>`; `equipWeapon` levels up the weapon (temporary) and `applyMineralChoiceReward` levels it up permanently; expose `getWeaponLevel(id)` / `getWeaponDef(id)` returning the **level-resolved** definition.
3. **Apply the leveled definition in the shared auto-fire path.** `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` uses the resolved definition for pattern/colour/size/lifetime/speed, so game and gyms inherit the same behaviour; new variables (e.g. piercing/damage/AoE) are applied through the shared core.
4. **Fire-rate upgrade quantisation.** Fire-rate upgrades map to the nearest valid beat subdivision (or otherwise remain on-grid) so AC6 holds.
5. **Permanent mineral leveling.** The mineral choice offers level-up options/levels for weapons and applies them permanently.
6. **HUD + gym.** Show per-weapon level in the HUD; add a weapon-leveling gym scene demonstrating temporary (drop) and permanent (choice) leveling, with the full-catalogue help overlay pattern.
7. **Docs.** Update GDD §4.4/§4.5, README and code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — extend catalogue with the upgrade spec and level resolver; keep `createBulletsFromHeading` signature/back-compat where possible.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` *(new)* — pure level-curve maths (diminishing returns, caps, monotonicity) and variable application.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — per-weapon level map, level-up on `equipWeapon`, `getWeaponLevel`, level-resolved `getWeaponDef`, reset semantics.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — consume the resolved definition; apply piercing/damage/AoE in the shared path.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — permanent weapon level-up on choice.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` / `src/powerups/types.ts` — offer level-up options / reflect levels.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — per-weapon level readout.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` *(new)* — demonstration gym (+ index registration).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4/§4.5 updates; `README.md` — feature/doc pointer.
- Tests alongside each module: `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts`, `weapons.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.*.test.ts`, gym tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (high):** the variable space is intentionally large. Mitigation: MVP slice implements ≥ 4 variables; the rest are specified in AC1 and shipped via follow-up child items.
- **Beat-grid regression (medium):** fire-rate upgrades could create off-grid intervals. Mitigation: quantise to subdivisions; AC6 test.
- **Balance / runaway scaling (medium):** indefinite levels risk trivialising the game. Mitigation: finite caps + diminishing returns; tunables in `src/core/rules.ts`.
- **Gym/game divergence (medium):** duplication would break the parity convention. Mitigation: resolve levels in the shared core; equivalence/duplicate-body tests.
- **Reset ambiguity (low):** does the Reset drop clear a weapon's level or only its active timer? **Assumption:** Reset clears *timed activation* but retains *levels* (levels are run-scoped progress); documented and tunable.
- **"4 offers" discrepancy (low):** the producer's answer referenced "choose from 4 offers" while GDD/code currently offer **3**. **Assumption:** keep the existing 3-offer mechanism unchanged for intake; flagged as an Open Question below rather than silently changed.
- **Research references:** Vampire Survivors (per-weapon levels with discrete per-level effects/evolutions), Risk of Rain 2 (stacking multiplicative item effects, status/proc), Brotato (tiered weapons, level-up choice from random offers), Mothwegunship (bullet-pattern/weapon-feel reference). *(Mothwegunship is the least-documented reference in this environment; it is treated as a feel/pattern reference to research during design.)*

## Related work

- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship's hold and grant a power-up choice (the permanent-upgrade path this epic extends).
- **AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX** — Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support (the extension point for weapon level-up offers).
- **AH-0MUOOB3OR001V8CD** — Area of effect weapons (in-progress; supplies the AoE variable).
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene (precedent for the demonstration gym).
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** — Make weapons both cumulative and time out (current timed semantics this epic layers levels onto).
- **AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG** — Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant (constrains fire-rate upgrades).
- **AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR** — Extract auto-fire with `onWeaponFired` hook (shared `_autoFire` path to extend).
- **AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B** — Bullets always fall on the beat (AC6 invariant).
- **AH-0MUPP1Q7S009NFHE** — The default weapon pickup should not reset weapons (collection semantics).
- **AH-0MUGY89LE006WVDQ** — Scene-level tests: verify real bullet spawns land on grid ticks (test precedent).
- **GDD** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (power-ups/weapons) and §4.5 (minerals, hold, choice).
- *Automated report:* see "Related work (automated report)" in the final description (find-related skill).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded 2026-10-02 via the intake interview. All answers from the **Producer**.

- **Q1: Scope — design vs implementation?**
  — **Answer (Producer):** *Implementation.* The epic implements the system (research/design are part of the work), not a standalone design document.
- **Q2: Target — MVP or post-MVP?**
  — **Answer (Producer):** *MVP, partial* — no need to implement everything, just enough to demonstrate the concept.
- **Q3: Leveling mechanics — preferred approach?**
  — Offering: A) Vampire Survivors style (weapon levels with per-level effects); B) Risk of Rain 2 / Brotato style (stacking random stat upgrades); C) hybrid; D) other.
  — **Answer (Producer):** *A* — Vampire Survivors style weapon levels.
- **Q4: Scope of weapon variables?**
  — **Answer (Producer):** *Yes* — plan for as many options as possible; the MVP only needs enough to demonstrate the concept. (Fixtures the ≥ 12-variable catalogue in AC1 and the ≥ 4 implemented variables in AC4.)
- **Q5: Progression integration?**
  — Offering: during a level / between levels / separate layer.
  — **Answer (Producer):** *During* — leveling happens during a level, as weapon collection currently does.
- **Q6: Maximum levels per weapon?**
  — **Answer (Producer):** *Indefinite, with diminishing returns.*
- **Q7: Player choice vs automatic?**
  — **Answer (Producer):** *As it is now* — collect power-ups for temporary upgrades (randomly spawned and collected); minerals for permanent upgrades (choose from 4 offers).

### Open questions

- **RESOLVED (planning, 2026-10-02):** Q7 mentioned "choose from 4 offers" but the GDD (§4.5) and `src/powerups/choice.ts` currently offer **3** mineral-choice options. **Producer decision: keep 3.** The existing 3-offer mechanism is unchanged.
- **RESOLVED (planning, 2026-10-02):** MVP upgrade-variable selection. **Producer decision: all four proposed variables approved** — fire rate, projectile count, bullet size, AoE radius.
- **OPEN QUESTION (minor, plan):** Q2 specifically asks *what the "Reset drop" is* before deciding its leveling semantics. **Assumption remains:** the Reset drop clears *timed activation* but retains *weapon levels* (levels are run-scoped progress). Awaiting producer confirmation (see plan comment for the explanation).

### Process notes

- The `skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` helper referenced by the intake skill is **not present** in this environment's installed skills (`~/.pi/agent/skills/skill/` contains only `__pycache__`). AC-coverage verification was therefore performed manually: this epic has **no children** yet, and the ACs above cover design, temporary path, permanent path, parity, scaling, grid invariant, UX/gym, testing, docs and suite — no uncovered scope identified.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUGY89LE006WVDQ** – Scene-level tests: verify real bullet spawns land on grid ticks (completed)
- **AH-0MTHG51UN001ZAZW** – Formation and shot-pattern registries (completed)
- **AH-0MTHG5BSP006A81R** – Gym index discovers all enemy configs (completed)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muayb8eh005rj8b, 0mubvgi62004ed9q, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+446 more)

## Summary

Replace gym `_onWaveTimeout()` to persist survivors and spawn a fresh formation after the 3s countdown alongside them.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On timeout, surviving gym enemies remain alive — no detonation.
2. After 3s respawn countdown, a fresh formation spawns alongside survivors.
3. Survivors continue moving and attacking during the countdown.
4. Both survivors and the fresh formation must be cleared for the gym to advance.

## Key Files

## Implementation Notes

- Rewrite `_onWaveTimeout()`: filter survivors (exclude asteroids), do NOT call `detonateWaveTimeoutSurvivors()`.
- Create `_respawnWithCarriedSurvivors()` method:
  - Save alive survivor entities (their current state)
  - Clear enemy bullets (as `respawnFormation` does)
  - Clear in-flight glide
  - Destroy old (dead) entities, rebuild formation
  - Re-add saved survivors to scene at their current positions
  - Restore survivor `shootEnabled` state
- During countdown, survivors update normally (they are not in `this.entities` but are still added to the scene)
- The fresh formation uses `this.config` to rebuild

# Level-curve resolver with property tests

## Summary
Implement the pure mathematical module for weapon level curves: diminishing returns, caps, monotonicity, and the level-resolver function that maps (weaponId, level) to per-variable stats.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Module src/utils/weaponLevels.ts exports a resolveWeaponAtLevel(weaponId, level) function returning per-variable stats.
- AC2: The module defines a WeaponUpgradeSpec type and catalogue covering >= 12 tunable variables (fire rate, projectile count, spread/pattern angle spread, bullet size, bullet speed, lifetime, damage, piercing, bounce, homing strength, AoE radius, status effect chance, chain count, crit multiplier, split-on-hit, knockback force).
- AC3: Each variable uses a diminishing-returns curve (e.g. base * (1 - exp(-k * level)) or similar) with a finite asymptotic cap.
- AC4: Property tests verify monotonic non-decreasing effective values across levels 1..100 for all variables.
- AC5: Property tests verify that no variable exceeds its cap at any level.
- AC6: Property tests verify that the curve is strictly increasing (or constant-at-cap) -- no decreases at higher levels.

## Key Files
- src/utils/weaponLevels.ts (new) -- curve maths, spec catalogue, resolver

# Spawning enemies enter from a wormhole and grow from 1 pixel to their full size

## Problem statement

Currently, enemies spawn instantaneously — they simply appear at their formation position. We want a cinematic spawn sequence: a wormhole opens, enemies grow from 1 pixel to their full size, and the wormhole fades out. During this sequence the player cannot interact with the enemies.

## Users

- **Primary:** Players experiencing the game — the spawn animation improves visual polish and clarity of the enemy entry moment.
- **Secondary:** Gym scene users — parity requires the same animation in all gym scenes that spawn enemies.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Wormhole opens** — A wormhole visual effect appears at the enemy spawn position and animates open over 1 second.
2. **Enemy growth** — Each spawned enemy starts at 1 pixel (scale 0.01) and grows to its full configured size over 1.5 seconds using a smooth easing.
3. **Wormhole closes** — After the enemy growth animation completes (1.5 s after growth starts), the wormhole fades/disappears over 0.5 seconds.
4. **Spawn protection window** — During the full spawn sequence (1 s open + 1.5 s grow + 0.5 s close = 3 s), the following restrictions apply:
   - Player bullets cannot destroy spawning enemies (they pass through or are ignored).
   - Spawning enemies cannot shoot at the player.
   - Spawning enemies cannot collide with the player ship or with minerals.
5. **Parity across scenes** — The same spawn animation is applied consistently to both `PlayScene` (the main game) and all gym scenes that spawn enemies (`GymEnemies` and related gym formation scenes).
6. **All tests pass** — The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The spawn animation must not change the spawn positions or timing of enemies — only the visual presentation and interaction state.
- The animation must work for all enemy types (Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Asteroid, Harvester).
- The wormhole VFX should be consistent with existing VFX patterns in `src/vfx/`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_spawnEnemy()` method needs modification to trigger the spawn animation sequence.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — enemy creation in gym scenes needs the same animation.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — base gym scene spawn logic may need updating.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — `createEnemyFromConfig()` may need to accept an optional growth animation flag.
- `src/vfx/` — new wormhole VFX module (e.g. `wormholeSpawn.ts`).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — documentation update for the new spawn mechanic.

## Related work

- AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123 — "Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen" (completed) — related spawn mechanic.
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V — "Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy deaths" (completed) — same VFX pattern/style, useful reference.
- Gym-parity convention in `AGENTS.md` — ensures gym and game spawning must stay in sync.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The wormhole visual can be implemented as a Phaser Graphics-based animation (similar to existing VFX).
- **Assumption:** Enemy entities support runtime scale modification (Phaser scale property).
- **Risk:** The spawn protection window must be carefully coordinated across all entity types (bullets, collisions, shooting).
- **Risk:** Gym scenes may have different spawn code paths; each needs to be identified and updated.
- **Scope creep:** Avoid adding extra wormhole VFX variants or sound effects unless explicitly requested.
